hooks.text: Male deep-sea anglerfish dissolve their own bodies to survive.
Female anglerfish grow up to sixty times larger than their mates.
A tiny male anglerfish permanently fuses into the body of a female.

title: Anglerfish: The Males That Fuse Into Females
description: Discover how tiny male deep-sea anglerfish permanently fuse into massive females, dissolving their own organs to share a single bloodstream.

beats.text: Male deep-sea anglerfish dissolve their own bodies to survive.
beats.visual: Deep-sea anglerfish female with attached male, Ceratias holboelli

beats.text: In the pitch-black deep sea, finding a mate is nearly impossible for the two hundred known species of anglerfish.
beats.visual: NOAA ROV video capture of the deep ocean bathypelagic zone

beats.text: Females use bioluminescent lures to attract prey and can swallow animals twice their own size.
beats.visual: Bioluminescent esca and illicium of a humpback anglerfish, Melanocetus johnsonii

beats.text: Moving down the ladder, male Photocorynus spiniceps are among the smallest vertebrates at about seven millimeters long.
beats.visual: Male Photocorynus spiniceps specimen attached to a female

beats.text: That makes the massive female up to sixty times larger than her tiny mate.
beats.visual: Scientific illustration comparing female and male anglerfish sizes

beats.text: When a male finally finds a female, he latches on with his teeth to begin a permanent transformation.
beats.visual: Close-up of a male anglerfish latching onto female skin

beats.text: His eyes and internal organs slowly wither away until only his reproductive organs remain.
beats.visual: Anatomical drawing of a parasitic male fused to a female

beats.text: He can fuse into her body because he lacks the immune genes that would normally reject foreign tissue.
beats.visual: Microscopic view of fused blood vessels between two anglerfish

beats.text: This dependence on her blood supply is why.
beats.visual: Deep-sea anglerfish female swimming with parasitic males, Ceratias holboelli
